key_insight: DiffEEG uses self-supervised diffusion pre-training plus reinforcement learning fine-tuning to learn strong EEG representations when labeled seizure data are scarce and imbalanced.
clinical_relevance: The approach may improve seizure monitoring by better detecting rare ictal events while keeping performance usable under patient-wise testing.
method: Pre-trains a 9.6M-parameter 1D U-Net with multi-head self-attention on 1.3M unlabeled EEG segments.
Uses denoising diffusion to learn generic EEG features without manual labels.
Applies RL-based decision-layer fine-tuning to directly optimize F1-score for rare seizure classes.
evidence_signal: On 279 patients with leave-one-fold-out evaluation, the model reached 81% accuracy and 85% weighted F1 for binary detection, and 61% accuracy with 59% F1 for 4-class seizure subtyping.
watch_item: The strong results depend on a specific dataset and evaluation setting, so real-world generalization and clinical integration still need external validation.
paper_title: DiffEEG: A Self-Supervised Denoising Diffusion Model for Learning EEG Generic Representations
